comment: The definition is useful and simple but remains health-agency and asset centred. A DPI should be judged not only by reuse across agency functions, but by whether it creates public value across a health ecosystem that includes people, communities, public and private providers, and subnational actors. The definition also omits the complementarity of assisted and non-digital routes, which are important where digital identity, literacy, connectivity or devices are uneven. This is consistent with the Universal DPI Safeguards Framework: https://www.dpi-safeguards.org/framework

public.suggestedRevision: Revise the definition to describe DPI-H as an evolving, publicly governed socio-technical infrastructure that enables multiple health and public-health functions across societal actors. DPI-H is complementary to equitable assisted/non-digital access functions. DPI-H should create public value across the network of health stakeholders.
